A1.justification: Both PDFs are complete 31-page versions of ANTIC. Their corresponding text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–K support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original compression, reconstruction, temporal-selection, and runtime experiments on 2D Kolmogorov flows and 3D binary-black-hole simulations, including extensive appendix results.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results in the main text and appendices, with a corrected spectral-selector plot in Appendix H.

M1.justification: The physics-aware temporal selector, continual neural-field fine-tuning, and LoRA updates are unchanged. Sections 3–4 and Algorithms 1–3 retain the same components and procedures.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same Kolmogorov-flow and BSSN binary-black-hole simulations, resolution sweeps, and temporal regimes. The corrected 2048² spectral-selector panel represents an already included evaluation.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged across the compression, training-strategy, temporal-selector, and regulator comparisons. Spectral entropy was already evaluated in Appendix H; its revised plot does not introduce a comparator.

E3.justification: The reported simulation configurations, model sizes, training settings, snapshot windows, and evaluation metrics are unchanged. The revised spectral-selector output does not document a change to its evaluation protocol.

E4.justification: Appendix H's existing analysis of temporal-selector sensitivity across resolutions receives a revised 2048² spectral-selector selection and jump-size trace in Fig. 13b. This changes one supporting example; the other ablations, reconstruction analyses, and scaling studies are retained.

E5.justification: The five-snapshot summaries and uncertainty displays in Tables 2–3 and Fig. 4, together with timing variability in Table 9, are unchanged. No seed, repeated-run, or statistical-estimation information is added or revised.

E6.justification: Fig. 13b changes the spectral selector's reported retention at 2048² from 2.00% to 2.50%, with a different selection/jump pattern and a displayed maximum jump of 142 instead of 230. Table 8 already reports 25 retained frames out of 1,000, or 2.50%, in both versions. Other results are unchanged.

T1.justification: The residual-update formulation, physics-metric definitions, BSSN derivations, and complexity/scaling arguments are retained. No mathematical assumption, derivation, theorem, or proof is added or substantively revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions and claims about combined temporal/spatial compression, reconstruction fidelity, and continual fine-tuning efficiency.

C2.justification: Appendix H retains its interpretation of physics-agnostic selectors' failure modes despite the corrected panel. Section 6 preserves the same limitations concerning latency, derivative fidelity, PDE-specific metrics, and unvalidated off-grid generalization.

D1.justification: Architecture, optimizer, hyperparameter, data-generation, hardware, and software disclosures are unchanged. The ANTIC repository link also remains the same.

R1.justification: The cited works and research-positioning arguments are unchanged. Four retained bibliography entries lose printed URLs, but no cited work or substantive relationship to prior research is added or removed.

P1.justification: The author name changes from Gianluca Galleti to Gianluca Galletti, the template running header becomes the paper title, and the preprint footer becomes an ICML proceedings notice. The scientific prose and section organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Fig. 13b is redrawn with different retained-snapshot markers, a revised jump-size curve, and an upper jump-size axis label changing from 230 to 142. Header/footer changes and shortened bibliography entries produce limited text reflow; no figures or tables are added or removed.

improvement.justification: v2 resolves the inconsistency between Fig. 13b and Table 8 by showing 2.50% spectral-selector retention at 2048², matching the existing 25-of-1,000 result. Corrected author spelling and replacement of the template header also improve presentation. These are limited, verifiable gains in reporting consistency; the scientific scope and supporting experiments remain unchanged.
